body.statement:
Suppose that there exists at least one uniform acquisition certificate \(E\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1\). Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(n=|V|\). Then there is a lexicographically canonical accepting uniform certificate \(E^{\star}\) with at most \(k\) nonempty records, one owned transcript schema for each factor, no empty-ownership record, and cost no larger than that of any accepting uniform certificate. Every transcript has at most \(n\) strict restrictions and at most \(8(n+1)^2\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\rceil\) bits. Consequently,
\[
 N_{E^{\star}}\le B_{\mathrm{cert}}
 =k\bigl(m+L+k+n(1+L)\bigr)
 +8k(n+1)^2\left\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\right\rceil
 \le 8k(N_{\mathrm{in}}+1)^4,
\]
and \(\operatorname{Cost}(E^{\star})=\operatorname{Opt}\). Oracle replies are separately charged by \(N_{\mathcal O}\). No comparison with arbitrary nonuniform acquired collections is asserted.
body.justification: The bound separates compact existential certificate data from potentially large, explicitly charged oracle support replies.
body.gap: Fixed-source completeness provides no canonical polynomial bound on an endogenous physical acquisition certificate or its transcript schema.
body.consumer: The exact optimizer can bound certificate enumeration while reporting source-interface cost separately.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(E\) be any accepting uniform certificate.  By the certificate definition, after empty ownership masks are ignored, the nonempty masks form a partition of \([k]\).  There are therefore at most \(k\) nonempty records, and the total number of owned transcripts is exactly \(k\), one for each factor.

Delete every empty-ownership record.  Each branch of each factor retains its unique owning record, and that record's fixed protocol, slice, source, and transcript still succeed uniformly over the factor's branches.  The operational acceptance checks can therefore be repeated without any deleted record: the retained owned source itself witnesses every factor branch in the complete source loop.  Thus the reduced certificate is accepting.  Its distinct-protocol set is a subset of the old one, so nonnegativity of the binary-rational action costs gives weakly smaller cost.  Sorting and merging equal records preserves the decoded sources, ownership, and cost and yields the canonical representation.

For the size bound, a source set \(T\) has at most \(n\) vertices.  Lemma \(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) gives at most \(n\) strict restrictions.  Put
\[
 r=\left\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\right\rceil.
\]
Encode the number of steps in \(r\) bits and each of the at most \(n+1\) triples \((U_r,H_r,B_r)\) by three \(n\)-bit masks and one \(r\)-bit framing tag.  Literal identities are already fixed by the record's source and literal masks and the canonical literal table, so they need not be repeated in the transcript.  Since \(r\ge1\), this uses at most
\[
 r+(n+1)(3n+r)
 \le 8(n+1)^2r
\]
bits.  Each record has \(m+L+k+n(1+L)\) fixed-width bits.  There are at most \(k\) records and exactly \(k\) transcripts, whence
\[
 N_E\le
 k\bigl(m+L+k+n(1+L)\bigr)+8k(n+1)^2r
 =B_{\mathrm{cert}}.
\]

The self-delimiting structural input explicitly lists all vertices, actions, literals, and factors.  Hence, with \(N=N_{\mathrm{in}}\ge1\),
\[
 n,m,L,k\le N,
 \qquad
 \left\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\right\rceil\le N+2.
\]
Consequently the bracket multiplying \(k\) in \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) is at most
\[
 N^2+4N+8(N+1)^2(N+2)
 \le 8(N+1)^4.
\]
For the last inequality, subtracting the middle transcript term from the right side leaves \(8(N+1)^2(N^2+N-1)\), which is at least \(N^2+4N\) for every integer \(N\ge1\).  This proves \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\le8k(N_{\mathrm{in}}+1)^4\).

Starting from any accepting uniform certificate, the preceding reduction gives an accepting canonical string of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) and no greater cost.  There are finitely many binary strings of that length.  The nonempty set of accepted ones therefore has a minimum exact rational cost, and its finite set of minimizers has a lexicographically first member \(E^{\star}\).  Because every accepting uniform certificate is dominated by a member of this bounded set, \(\operatorname{Cost}(E^{\star})=\operatorname{Opt}\), and \(N_{E^{\star}}\le B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  The construction uses only the structural certificate bits; all oracle replies remain charged separately by \(N_{\mathcal O}\).
